purpose: Griseofulvin is used to treat fungal infections of the skin, hair, and nails. It works against infections like ringworm, athlete's foot, jock itch, and fungal nail infections. It is only for fungal infections and will not work on bacterial or viral infections.
how_it_works: Griseofulvin works by getting absorbed into your skin, hair, and nails, where it stops the fungus from growing and spreading. It basically interrupts the fungus's ability to reproduce and make new cells. Over time, as your body grows new healthy skin, hair, or nails, the infection clears up.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include headache, upset stomach, nausea, diarrhea, and dizziness. Some people notice skin sensitivity to sunlight, so be sure to use sunscreen outdoors. You may also feel tired or have trouble sleeping.
warnings: Let your doctor know if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as this medication can harm an unborn baby. Avoid alcohol while taking this medicine because it can cause a fast heartbeat, flushing, and nausea. People with lupus or liver problems should use this medication with caution. This medicine may make birth control pills less effective, so talk to your doctor about backup contraception. Do not stop taking it early even if you feel better — finishing the full course is important.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 500 mg taken by mouth once a day or split into smaller doses throughout the day. Taking it with a fatty meal like whole milk or ice cream helps your body absorb it better. Treatment can last from a few weeks to several months depending on the type and location of the infection.
